description.en: SDR-Bench evaluates LLM personalization in a two-party framework. It includes 6,279 customer success stories across 22 industries and ~200 enterprises, with a temporally constrained simulation to prevent data leakage. Scoring compares model-generated outreach against human outcomes.

evidence.snippet: We release SDR-Bench, a public corpus of 6,279 customer success stories spanning 22 industries and approximately 200 enterprises, served through a temporally constrained simulation that prevents future-data leakage.

claire_radar.motivation: Personalization, the act of varying a message to induce action from a specific receiver while keeping sender, channel, and time fixed, has a long tradition in psychology and marketing as a two-party problem in which sender and receiver have independent objectives.

claire_radar.paperTitle: Benchmarking the Personalization Capabilities of Large Language Models

source.title: Benchmarking the Personalization Capabilities of Large Language Models

claire_radar.whyItMatters: SDR-Bench addresses the gap in evaluating LLM personalization as a two-party problem, where generated messages must induce action in a third party. It provides a reproducible public benchmark for comparing model performance on this task, with validation against field deployment.
